clue.text: Inside the Gulag has them horror-struck

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: starts at the last two letters of Gulag, takes all of has, and ends on the first letter of them

explanation.surface: Prisoners in a Soviet labour camp are appalled by what they find there.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters bridge three words: the end of Gulag, all of has, and the first letter of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone struck with horror or shock.

clue.text: An extra put on to conclude university term (finally!)

indicators.note: takes the final letter of term

blocks.note: to add is to put on more
to end is to conclude
U = university
last letter of term

explanation.surface: An extra item is tacked on to round off the university term.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed exclamation reads like relief that term is over, but it is just the instruction to take the last letter of term.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an addendum is material added to a book or document.

clue.text: Lead compound found in home is bad for the hair

definitions.note: the definition describes the insect rather than naming it: a head louse is something bad for the hair

indicators.note: a compound mixes its elements, so the letters of lead are mixed
the mixed letters are placed inside home

blocks.note: a house is a home
LEAD rearranged, placed after the first letter of HOUSE

explanation.surface: A lead compound turned up in the house, and it is harmful to hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as chemistry, lead poisoning in the home, but lead is only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the parasite lives among the hairs of the scalp, which is why it is bad for them.

clue.text: Heavyweight sport taken up in bedroom usually

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top
the letters are inside the following words

blocks.note: the last two letters of bedroom and the first two of usually

explanation.surface: A heavyweight sport is usually played in the bedroom, a suggestive picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at something other than wrestling in the bedroom, which is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: Japanese wrestling between very heavy men.

clue.text: Italian bread strike reported by secret agents

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so we want a word said like batter

blocks.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency
to batter is to strike repeatedly

explanation.surface: Italian bakers go on strike, and spies are the ones who report it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is an industrial dispute; strike here is the verb to hit, not a walkout.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by type: a flat, open-textured white loaf from Italy.

clue.text: One real NHS reform could relieve congestion

definitions.note: the definition describes what inhalers do rather than naming them

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: I = one, the Roman numeral
anagram fodder with I

explanation.surface: A proper reform of the NHS could ease its overcrowding.
explanation.walkthrough: Congestion reads as crowded hospitals, but it is congestion of the chest. The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: these devices deliver medicine that clears blocked airways.

clue.text: Risqué writer has to make corrections

blocks.note: blue = indecent, as in a blue joke
a pencil is a thing that writes

explanation.surface: An author of racy books is made to revise the text.
explanation.walkthrough: Writer reads as a person, but it is the implement.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: editors once marked cuts and changes in blue crayon, so the verb means to edit.

clue.text: Musically all-inclusive

blocks.note: points to a term from a musical score
reads like a holiday package, but means every performer at once

explanation.surface: An all-inclusive deal, but for music.
explanation.walkthrough: Tutti is Italian for all; in a score it marks the passage where every player joins in.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical term: the Italian word for all marks where the full orchestra plays together.

clue.text: Congratulations have no place in financial examinations

indicators.note: the word for congratulations must do without the letters for place, so they are dropped

blocks.note: plaudits are praise
PL = place, the map abbreviation; removed from the front

explanation.surface: Nobody gets praised in a financial audit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a gloomy truth about accountants; place is just the two letters PL.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: official inspections of a firm's accounts.

clue.text: “Time” requires article before this rival

blocks.note: put THE in front of the answer and you get an old nickname for time
the straight definition

explanation.walkthrough: The old question "How goes the enemy?" means "What's the time?", so time is THE ENEMY.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an opponent one is set against.

clue.text: Empty bottles proverbially silent!

definitions.note: the second definition is an adjective phrase: those who are proverbially silent

blocks.note: slang for empties left after drinking
the proverb says they tell no tales

explanation.surface: Empties sit quietly after the party, the joke being that they say nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Dead men is informal British slang for empty bottles after a drinking session.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for empties, and the subject of the proverb about telling no tales.

clue.text: Troubled relative he would briefly welcome

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so HE'D takes the relative inside
said briefly, he would shrinks to the contraction HE'D

blocks.note: HE'D is the contraction of he would
an aunt is a relative; placed after the H

explanation.surface: A worried man would gladly receive a relative for a short stay.
explanation.walkthrough: Briefly looks like a word about the length of the visit; it only shortens he would.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: someone tormented by worries or memories has a haunted look.

clue.text: No score at end of game that’s much longer than 25

indicators.note: takes the last letter of game

blocks.note: nil = nothing, a score of zero
last letter of game

explanation.surface: A goalless game drags on far beyond twenty-five minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is the answer to 25 down, SEINE; the Nile is far longer than that river.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-reference: at over 6,600 km this African river dwarfs the Seine's 777 km.

clue.text: Dash around the shops – a trap for the unwary

indicators.note: the word for dash is placed around the shops, holding them inside

blocks.note: a sprint is a dash
a mall is a shopping centre; placed after the S

explanation.surface: Rushing round the shops, a shopper is warned of a hidden snare.
explanation.walkthrough: Dash around the shops reads as a hurried shopping trip; around is the container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by effect: terms tucked away in a contract catch out those who do not read them.

clue.text: Write letters guaranteed to get you transported

blocks.note: to spell is to write the letters of a word
bound to = certain to

explanation.surface: Writing letters is a sure way to be carried away.
explanation.walkthrough: Transported here means enraptured, not carried somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: transported means carried away with delight, as if under a spell.

clue.text: Pursues without energy, unfit, yet still takes over

indicators.note: the letters are not in fit order, so rearrange them

blocks.note: the fodder as printed
E = energy; removed

explanation.surface: A worn-out, unfit contender still manages a takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a spent chaser who wins anyway; the fodder is the word pursues itself, minus one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to seize a position or power wrongfully.

clue.text: Single variety of orange dates back centuries

definitions.note: the definition is a verb phrase describing the period rather than naming it

indicators.note: a variety of orange is its letters in a different arrangement

blocks.note: I = one
ORANGE rearranged

explanation.surface: A particular kind of orange has a history going back centuries.
explanation.walkthrough: Variety reads as a fruit cultivar; it is the anagram instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the prehistoric period after the Bronze Age lies many centuries back.

clue.text: German girl on trial that’s just for show

definitions.note: the definition describes what a glass case is for rather than naming it

blocks.note: G = German
a lass is a girl
a case is a trial in court

explanation.surface: A German woman's trial is a show trial.
explanation.walkthrough: Just for show sounds like a sham trial; it is literal: a glass case displays things.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a display cabinet exists to show things off.

clue.text: Toothless old PM hanging here?

blocks.note: Anthony Eden, British Prime Minister 1955-57
the Tate is a London art gallery where pictures hang

explanation.surface: A feeble former Prime Minister's portrait hangs in a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: Toothless reads as ineffectual, fitting a weak politician, but it is the literal definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical synonym from Latin dens, tooth: lacking teeth.

clue.text: Vague commonsense about mixing colour (seen in 6)

indicators.note: commonsense goes around the mixed colour
the letters of blue are mixed

blocks.note: nous is common sense
BLUE, the colour in 6 down BLUE PENCIL, rearranged and placed after the N

explanation.surface: Hazy sense applied to blending paint colours.
explanation.walkthrough: The colour is identified by pointing to 6 down, BLUE PENCIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: literally cloudy, hence indistinct or vague.

clue.text: English child I dressed up for Scottish party

indicators.note: dressing up changes appearance, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: E = English
anagram fodder with E

explanation.surface: An English child puts on fancy clothes for a party in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: A ceilidh is a Scottish or Irish evening of folk music and dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional word: the Gaelic name for a social evening of folk music and dancing.

clue.text: What pupils can do in surprising detail

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged into an unexpected order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Schoolchildren can do surprisingly detailed work.
explanation.walkthrough: Pupils are the ones in the eyes, not in the classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the pupils of the eyes widen in dim light.

clue.text: A branch’s most able people

blocks.note: as printed
DEPT is short for department, a branch of an organisation

explanation.surface: One branch of a firm holds its best staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s is read as is, giving DEPT'S.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: experts, people highly skilled at something.

clue.text: Selfish citizen who’s quickly left out

blocks.note: nimbly = quickly
L = left; removed

explanation.surface: A self-centred citizen is swiftly excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: A NIMBY ("not in my back yard") objects to local developments while accepting them elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by attitude: the acronym labels residents who put their own patch ahead of the community.

clue.text: Refuse cover

blocks.note: reads as the verb to decline, but it is the noun: rubbish
reads as insurance, but it is a literal lid

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a verb, refuse cover means decline insurance; it is the noun refuse, rubbish. A dustbin is a British rubbish bin.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal reading: the lid of a rubbish bin covers the refuse inside.

clue.text: Sensible-sounding flower

indicators.note: we want a word that sounds like a word for sensible

blocks.note: sane = sensible; the French river is said the same way

explanation.walkthrough: Flower is a thing that flows, a river, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: a flower is something that flows, here the river through Paris.

clue.text: Man out of Genesis in a Beatles audience

indicators.note: the answer is in the words that follow

blocks.note: the last two letters of Beatles and the first two of audience

explanation.surface: A former member of the band Genesis is spotted in a Beatles crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis looks like the rock band beside the Beatles; it is the first book of the Bible, where Esau appears.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by source: Jacob's twin brother appears in the Book of Genesis.

clue.text: Odd sights starting usually from outer space

indicators.note: takes the starting letter of each following word

blocks.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Strange sightings usually come from beyond Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay also describes the answer, since UFOs are supposedly from outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: unexplained objects seen in the sky.

clue.text: Proper centrally regulated flower

indicators.note: takes the central letters of regulated

blocks.note: prim = proper, strait-laced
middle three letters of reg(ULA)ted

explanation.surface: A tidily kept, properly controlled flower bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Unlike 25 down, this flower is a real bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: the primrose family of spring-flowering plants.

clue.text: One of the herd in New York city

blocks.note: a large wild ox that roams in herds
a city in New York State, on Lake Erie

explanation.surface: Someone is just another face in the New York crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: New York city looks like New York City itself; it is a city in the state of New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a herd animal, and the upstate city on Lake Erie.

clue.text: More stable flying aid acquired by pilot

indicators.note: the letters of aid fly about into a new order
the pilot takes the mixed letters inside

blocks.note: to steer is to pilot
AID rearranged, placed after STE

explanation.surface: A pilot takes on a flight aid that steadies the plane.
explanation.walkthrough: Pilot is a verb here, to steer, not the person in the cockpit.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative synonym: firmer, less likely to wobble.

clue.text: They escort drug addicts around hospital

blocks.note: users = drug addicts
H = hospital, as on road signs; placed after US

explanation.surface: Staff accompany drug addicts round the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a hospital ward scene; they escort is the definition, the rest wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by role: people who show others to their seats.
